description: The hashed mode of a decision event's arguments (docs/contracts/module-contract-v0.1.md, section 8.3): the HMAC-SHA-256, in lowercase hexadecimal, of the canonical JSON of section 4.10 of the arguments object as the tool receives it, with a key that the deployment holds. key is that key, in hexadecimal. Each case gives the arguments, as a JSON value in arguments or, where a parsed object cannot hold them, as their text in arguments_text. Arguments that have a canonical JSON come with it, in canonical_json, whose UTF-8 bytes are hashed, and with hmac_sha256, the value that the event records with the key's ID. Section 4.10 writes a number without a fraction or an exponent as its exact value, whatever its size, and any other from its value as a double, as RFC 8785 does. Arguments without a canonical JSON, because of a number with a fraction or an exponent that is not finite as a double, a member name that repeats or a string with a lone surrogate, at any depth, are recorded by their names alone, each once: names, and names_sha256, the SHA-256 in lowercase hexadecimal of the UTF-8 bytes of each name longer than 128 characters or with a lone surrogate, each lone surrogate replaced by U+FFFD, in place of the name. Both are compared as sets. Strings escape every character beyond printable ASCII, so that invisible ones show. The key is for tests only: it is the SHA-256 of "White Tower conformance test key: hashed-arguments. Never trust it outside tests.", so anyone can compute with it. Never configure it anywhere else.

cases.description: Text beyond ASCII, which RFC 8785 writes as it is, in UTF-8: letters with diacritics, Japanese, a character beyond the Basic Multilingual Plane (U+1D49C, a surrogate pair in UTF-16) and the line separator U+2028
cases.canonical_json: {"body":"first line second line","greeting":"こんにちは","signature":"𝒜","subject":"Réunion à Göteborg"}

cases.description: The characters that RFC 8785 escapes in a string, a quote, a backslash and the control characters, five of them with their short escapes and the others as \u with four lowercase hexadecimal digits; and those it writes as they are: the solidus, <, >, & and DEL

Nested objects and arrays: the members of every object sorted, at every depth, and the items of every array kept in their order, repeats and empty arrays and objects included; and the largest integer of I-JSON, 2^53 - 1
Members sorted by their UTF-16 code units: B before a, a before aa, aa before b, then U+00E9, then U+1F600 before U+FF61, which their code points, and their UTF-8 bytes, would put the other way

Integers beyond I-JSON's 2^53 - 1, written exactly, so that every stack computes the same HMAC: 2^64 - 1, the bound of an unsigned 64-bit ID, which a double rounds to 18446744073709552000; 2^53 + 1, which a double rounds to 2^53; and -2^63 - 1, below the signed 64-bit range

Numbers with a fraction or an exponent, written from their value as a double as RFC 8785 does: a whole one without a fraction (1.0 as 1, 1e3 as 1000, 1E20 in full), -0.0 as 0, 1e21 as 1e+21, 1.5e-7 with an exponent, and 1e-400, below the smallest double, as 0; and -0, without a fraction, as 0
A member name twice: no canonical JSON, so the names alone, each once
A member name twice deeper in the arguments: the names alone, those of the arguments object
A lone surrogate in a value, within an array: the names alone
A number with an exponent that is not finite as a double: the names alone

A lone surrogate in an argument name, which an event cannot write: the names alone, that name as the SHA-256 of its UTF-8 bytes with each lone surrogate replaced by U+FFFD. The name is a low surrogate, a high surrogate and id: the two surrogates are not a pair, so each becomes U+FFFD, and the bytes hashed are ef bf bd ef bf bd 69 64

The names alone, after a member name twice, at the bound of 128 characters: a name of 127 letters and U+1D49C, 128 characters but 131 bytes in UTF-8 and 129 code units in UTF-16, is recorded as it is, and a name of 129 letters as its SHA-256
